rows.speaker: R
rows.claim: After establishing prophecy in verse 38, these verses ground it in divine origin; prophets confront false gods, as Joseph did.
rows.anchor: v. 39 seeks to establish the basis of prophecy, namely, its Divine Origin

rows.speaker: R
rows.claim: The rhetorical choice between many lords and God points to the fissures and ruin plurality would bring, versus the order and beauty made possible by the One God.
rows.anchor: if there were more than one god, the cosmic order would contain fissures and would go to ruin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 40 turns from the necessity of oneness to the duty to worship the one true God rather than idols, which are merely human-given names.
rows.anchor: false gods are nothing more than the names assigned to them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to worship only God echoes another verse; the upright religion formula links to two other passages.
rows.anchor: God’s Command that you worship none but Him is analogous to 17:23

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʾwīl etymologically means returning something to its origin; Quranic usages include interpreting equivocal verses and explaining unclear events.
rows.anchor: etymologically conveys the sense of bringing something back to its origin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Islamic thought taʾwīl can mean esoteric reading of a verse’s inner sense, contrasted with tafsīr’s outward sense, though the distinction is flexible; al-Ṭabarī uses taʾwīl in his commentary title.
rows.anchor: the spiritual or esoteric hermeneutics that reveals the inner meanings of a Quranic verse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥlām here is synonymous with ruʾyā in verse 43; the notables call the king’s vision confused, false dreams arising from the soul or demonic inspiration and lacking objective reality.
rows.anchor: Dreams translates aḥlām, which in this verse is a synonym for ruʾyā

rows.speaker: Kl
rows.claim: The notables may mean they cannot interpret false dreams specifically, or more likely that they cannot interpret dreams generally.
rows.anchor: their inability to interpret dreams in general
